column2: Twice five, tenth, seventh, third and thirteenth; in Revati, Rohini, Indra's, Agni's, Hasta, Mitra's and the Uttaras,
one should sow seeds, even one desiring prosperity, except Mandara. In Revati, Hasta, Mula, Shravana, Bhaga and Mitra's,
in the ancestral and divine and Soma's, cutting grain at Mrigashira's rising; in Hasta, Chitra, Punarvasu, Svati, Revati and the three Shravana,
in a fixed ascendant, on Thursday, then Friday and Wednesday; in Bharani, Punarvasu, Magha, Jyeshtha and the Uttaras one should cause entry.

Om, to the giver of wealth, lord of all wealth, give me wealth, svaha. Om, in the new year, goddess Ila, increaser of the world, desire-form, give me wealth, svaha. Written on a leaf and placed in a heap of grain it increases grain. In the three Purvas, Vishakha, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha,
in these six the wise should know the taking out of grain. At the consecration of temples, groves, wells and the like, when the Sun faces north,
when the Sun is in Gemini, from the new moon the twelfth lunar day; always then Chakrapani's sleeping should be done.
When the Sun is in Leo and Libra, from new moon two twelfths; first Indra's arising and Hari's awakening in order,
likewise when the Sun is in Virgo, Durga's arising and the eighth; when in the three-quarter stars the lunar day Bhadra occurs,
on Tuesday, Sunday or Saturday, it should be known as Tripushkara. In all works the purity of the moon and stars is to be accepted.
The moon in the birth sign, third, sixth, seventh, tenth and eleventh — for those one should declare it auspicious;
in the bright fortnight the second, fifth and ninth are good. The stars called friend, great friend, accomplisher, prosperity, safety and the like:
by birth one attains death, by danger loss of wealth; in Pratyari know death; in Nidhana he goes to the five elements.
From the dark eighth day up to the bright eighth day, for that time the moon is waned; full thereafter is remembered.
When the Sun is in Taurus or Gemini and Jupiter in the moon's or Indra's star, a full moon on Thursday is called the Great Jyeshthi.
In Indra's, with Jupiter and moon, and the Sun in Prajapatya, the full moon of Jyeshtha month is called Mahajyeshthi.
In the interval of Svati, in Yantra-nishtha, one should raise Indra's banner; at the foot of Hari's star and in Ashvini, at the end of a week, one should dismiss.
At the eclipse of the sun by Rahu, all gifts equal gold, all Brahmins equal Brahma, all water equals the Ganga.
Dhvankshi, Mahodari, Ghora, Manda, Mandakini, Rakshasi — in order from the Sun the transits are remembered by these names.
If in Balava, Kaulava, Naga or Taitila karana the Sun rising transits, then the people will be happy.
In Gara, Vava, Vanija, Vishti, Kimstughna, Shakuni he goes; by the king's fault this world is troubled together with prosperity.
When the Sun transits asleep in a four-footed Vishti Vanijya, there is famine, royal war, and doubt between spouses.
At conception on the birth-star, in illness there will be affliction and the like. In Krittika nine days, three nights, and in Rohini;
Mrigashira five nights; in Ardra loss of life; in Punarvasu and Pushya seven nights is prescribed;
nine nights likewise in Ashlesha; up to the cremation ground in Magha; two months in Purva Phalguni, three-five in the Uttaras;
in Hasta, Chitra is seen, a fortnight of affliction; two months in Svati; Vishakha twenty days;
in Mitra ten days; in Jyeshtha only a fortnight; in Mula no release; Purvashadha three-five;
Uttara twenty days; two months in Shravana; Dhanishtha a fortnight; in Varuna's ten days;
no release in Bhadrapada; in the Uttaras three-five; Revati ten nights; and Ashvini a day and night.
The period of ten years for the lame; nineteen by Jupiter's aspect; Rahu twelve years; Venus twenty-one.
In Bharani there is loss of life; by Gayatri oblation it is auspicious; with five grains, sesame, ghee and the rest, gift of a cow to a Brahmin brings peace.
The period of the Sun is six years; of the Moon fifteen; of Mars eight; of Mercury seventeen.
Smeared with sixty palas, sixty lipta is a day and night; at the rising of the fifth half: child, adolescent, young, old;
by whichever rising there is death, by that its setting by eleventh parts; at the entry of lineage there is breaking, with death, or the fifth.
The wheel of the rising of breath, and in the Saturn wheel the rising of the half-month planets in order; by fifteen divisions the Saturn portion gives death.
The Saturn wheel removes ten thousand arbudas; thirteen lakhs is the measure in the tortoise form.
From Magha to Krittika the end, in that region's end while Saturn stands; the tortoise wheel; in the Rahu wheel one should draw seven above and seven below.
In the northwest and southwest, from the southeast of the full moon; the new moon in the northwest; Rahu is of the form of the lunar day.
One should write Ra in the right part and Ha in the northwest; Ka and the rest from pratipada, and Sa in the southwest again.
At Rahu's face there is breaking — thus Rahu is declared. Vishti in the fire on the full moon; Karani third in Indra's;
Ghora in the south on the seventh; on the tenth Raudra in the north; on the fourteenth in the northwest; on the fourth in the west;
on the bright eighth in the south; on the eleventh one should avoid strongly: Raudra, Shveta, Maitra, Sarabhata,
Savitri, Virochana, Jayadeva, Abhijit, Ravana, Vijaya, Nandi and Varuna,
Yama, Saumya and Bhava at the end — the fifteen muhurtas. In Raudra one should do fierce acts; in Shveta bathing and the like;
in Maitra a girl's marriage and other auspicious acts; in Sarabhata; in Savitra installation and the like; in Virochana a king's rite;
in Jayadeva one should do victory; in Ravana war-work; in Vijaya agriculture and trade; tying a turban in Nandi;
in Varuna tanks and the like; in Yama destructive work; in Saumya gentle acts; the ascendant is by day and night.
Yogas are inauspicious by name, and yogas are auspicious by name alone. Rahu from Indra, the wind, from Vayu south, from Yama Shiva,
from Shiva the water, from the water fire, from fire Soma, thence three; then it destroys the transit, moving four ghatikas.
The Rahu wheel: Chandi, Indrani, Varahi, Mushali, Girikarnika, Bala, Atibala, Kshiri, Mallika, Jati, Yuthika —
one should wear them as available; and white arka, Shatavari, Guduchi, Vaguri, divine herbs worn for victory.

Om, homage to Bhairava, sword-and-axe-handed, Om Hrum, destroyer of obstacles, Om Hrum phat — by this very mantra the tying of the crest and the rest brings victory. Tilaka, collyrium, incense, anointing,
bathing, drinking, oils — hear the yoga-powder. Shubhaga, realgar, orpiment with lac-juice,
mixed with a young woman's milk, a tilaka on the forehead subdues; Vishnukranta, Sarpakshi, Sahadeva, rochana,
ground with goat's milk, the tilaka is subduing; priyangu, saffron, kushtha, mohini, tagara, ghee,
that tilaka subdues; rochana, red sandal, turmeric, realgar, orpiment, priyangu, mustard,
mohini, harita, kranta, sahadevi, shikha — ground with citron juice, a tilaka on the forehead subdues;
even gods with Indra come under control, what of petty men? Manjishtha, red sandal, katkanda, vilasini,
with punarnava, this ointment of the Sun subdues; sandal, nagapushpa, manjishtha, tagara, vacha,
lodhra, priyangu, turmeric, mamsi and oil are subduing.
The cruel power has the seed ī; the Hara-seed is of the form of fire; knowledge is equal Gandhari; and power is remembered as the burning one.
Peace belongs to water-touchers; Udana, the moving action; Om called beyond-peace; the leader-hand of the sound "kha."
The five groups of vowels arose: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn in order; the A and the rest, the Ka and the rest placed below.
This is the root; therefore all moving and unmoving is known. I shall tell the seat of knowledge: Om is called Shiva;
Uma, Soma, himself Shakti, Vama, Jyeshtha and Raudri; Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra in order; the three qualities beginning with creation;
the three jewel-channels: gross, subtle, supreme and beyond; one should contemplate him white, releasing supreme nectar;
one should contemplate that oneself as being floated day and night; ageless-ness comes, goddess, and one attains Shiva-hood.
One should place the limbs on the thumb and the rest, the eye in the middle, then in the body; having worshipped Mrityunjaya, one becomes victorious in battle and the like.
Void, without abode, sound; one should touch touch slantingly bowed; the upward motion of form is said, of water resting below;
smell, free of all places and in the middle the root; the bulb standing at the navel-root, adorned with Shiva's form;
by the arrangement of power the moon, sun and Hari are established there; joined with the ten winds, adorned with the five subtle elements,
like the fire of time, shining, of the nature of Shiva; that is the life of the world of beings, of the unmoving and moving;
when that is lost I consider it dead, in the mantra-seat of the nature of air.
By the strength of the five groups victory in battle comes; hear it. A, Ā, Ka, Cha, Ṭa, Ta, Pa, Ya, Sha — the first group is stated;
I, Ī, Kha, Chha, Ṭha, Tha, Pha, Ra, Sha — the second group; U, Ū, Ga, Ja, Ḍa, Da, Ba, La, Sa — the third group;
E, Ai, Gha, Jha, Ḍha, Dha, Bha, Va, Sa — the fourth group; O, Au, Am, Ah, Ṅa, Ña, Ṇa, Na, Ma — the fifth group.

The letters at a man's rise are forty-five. Child, adolescent, young, old, and death by name; self-afflicted, drying, indifferent, and Kalaka. Krittika, pratipada and Mars are remembered as giving gain to oneself:
the sixth, Mars, Magha is affliction; Ardra and the eleventh, Mars; death, Magha, second, Mercury; gain, Ardra and seventh.
In Mercury loss; Bharani, Mercury; Shravana such a time; Jupiter for gain; the third and Purva Phalguni.
Jupiter, the eighth, Dhanishtha, Ardra; Jupiter, Ashlesha, thirteenth. In death Venus, the fourth; Purva Bhadrapada for prosperity;
Purvashadha and the ninth — Venus becomes an afflicter. Bharani born of beings, Venus, Yama's staff, causes loss.
Krittika and the fifth: Saturn; for gain the lunar day is stated; Ashlesha and tenth, Saturn: the yoga becomes an afflicter;
Magha, Saturn and full moon: the yoga is remembered as bringing servitude. The lunar-day yoga: eastern, northern, fire, southwest, south, wind and moon;
Brahma and the others are the aspects, beginning with the first and ninth; planets and the rest seen with signs are remembered for success.
The four beginning with Aries — pots; victory in a full one, otherwise death. The Sun and others, empty and full, should be so given in order.
